case_identification.title: Cold-Chain Fulfillment Center — Capacity Scaling (unexpected demand increase)

case_inputs.brief: For the cold-chain fulfillment center operated by a metropolitan public agency, plan a capacity upgrade while protecting service quality following unexpected demand increase. Baseline capacity: 1,190 units/day. Deliver at least 8.5% improvement within 3 months under CAD 866,000 capital limit; installation restricted to weekends. Select a technically justified alternative and test what happens if performance falls 15%.
case_inputs.decision_question: For the cold-chain fulfillment center operated by a metropolitan public agency, plan a capacity upgrade while protecting service quality following unexpected demand increase. Baseline capacity: 1,190 units/day. Deliver at least 8.5% improvement within 3 months under CAD 866,000 capital limit; installation restricted to weekends. Select a technically justified alternative and test what happens if performance falls 15%.
case_inputs.objective: At least 8.5% improvement in capacity scaling within 3 months.
case_inputs.suggested_analysis: queueing, capacity calculation and bottleneck analysis

problem_diagnosis.core_bottleneck: Capacity Scaling sits at 1,190 units/day and must move 8.5% within 3 months under CAD $866,000 (metropolitan public agency; disruption: unexpected demand increase).
root_causes: Binding constraint hypothesis: one stage or subsystem limits capacity scaling; confirm with queueing, capacity calculation and bottleneck analysis before committing capital.
Variability, not average capacity, drives the gap: measure cycle/load variance and its share of lost performance.
Control and information gap: performance is managed on lagging data, so deviations are corrected late.
Delivery constraint shaping the solution space: installation restricted to weekends.
